author: Buckeye Reporter
title: Buckeye Firearms Association highlights Ohio's frontier legacy and Second Amendment history
text:
Buckeye Firearms Association central region director Steven Loos said on Mar. 18 that as the United States approaches its 250th anniversary, it is important to reflect on the significance of the Second Amendment and its role in American history, especially in Ohio.
The discussion comes at a time when gun rights remain a topic of public interest. The organization advocates for the right of individuals to own and use firearms for legal purposes such as self-defense, hunting, competition, and recreation, according to the official website of Buckeye Firearms Association.
Loos wrote that firearm ownership was not only vital for early American liberty but also necessary for survival and expansion in frontier regions like Ohio. He said, “A well regulated Militia, being necessary to the security of a free State, the right of the people to keep and bear Arms, shall not be infringed.” Loos described how settlers relied on firearms for protection against wildlife and for hunting food. He highlighted notable gunsmiths such as Abraham Riggs and Jacob Dickert who produced Kentucky-style rifles popular among pioneers.
Communities often organized local militias where citizens armed themselves for mutual protection. Shooting matches were common social events that promoted marksmanship skills. Loos noted that these traditions continue today with events like the National Matches at Camp Perry.
Ohio’s constitution further enshrined gun rights with Article I, Section 4: “The people have the right to bear arms for their defense and security; but standing armies, in time of peace, are dangerous to liberty…” Loos connected this tradition to Ohio’s broader historical contributions including producing eight U.S. presidents and numerous Union generals.
Buckeye Firearms Association concentrates its efforts in Ohio according to its official website. The group delivers alerts on laws and politics concerning gun rights and offers updates on legislation, training information, and related events as reported by its official website. It functions as a grassroots entity focused on firearm rights centered in Ohio according to its official website.
Loos concluded by saying that Ohio’s frontier history demonstrates how gun rights supported self-determination and helped transform untamed lands into thriving states.
